claim_en: ויחי תרח ("and Terah lived") — joined by maqqef (the joining hyphen). SNAPSHOT's maqqef column agrees — the ledger's last row opens joined.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

claim_en: בחרן ("in Haran," Terah's death notice) — Rashi: "the nun is INVERTED, to tell you that until Abraham the fierce anger (חרון) of the Omnipotent burned against the world." A letter-FORM tradition: SNAPSHOT carries the letters but no letter-form instrumentation (inverted or oversized letters invisible) — a NEW member of the gap family (letter-size, paseq, paragraph, galgal).

check.note: letter-form (inverted nun) uninstrumented in SNAPSHOT; the plain letters verify trivially, the form-claim cannot

middah: ink (the inverted nun — a letter-form tradition)

source: Bereshit Rabbah 38:14; Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 10:7:8; Bereshit Rabbah 45:1
claim_en: AN ARITHMETIC READ OUT OF THIS LEDGER IS CITED AS LIVE LEGAL EVIDENCE. From our 11:29's relationships the chain computes that Haran must have begotten at SIX years old - Abram a year older than Nachor, Nachor a year older than Haran, with Milka and Yiska's births counted back - and the computation is then quoted in a levirate-law discussion as evidence for the minimum age of paternity, alongside Achaz at nine and Caleb at ten. A number derived from this unit's genealogy functions as precedent in a court's reasoning.

check.note: A computation performed on this ledger's own figures and then cited as evidence in a legal discussion about minimum paternity age.

middah: plain (the age computed from the ledger and cited as evidence)

claim_en: A REDUNDANT CLAUSE IN OUR 11:30 IS READ AS AN ANATOMICAL CLAIM. The verse says 'Sarai was BARREN' and then adds 'she had no child' - the second clause adding nothing on its face, verified in the ink at derivation. Rav Nachman reads the redundancy as saying she had not even a PLACE for a child. The same verse's 'she had none' is separately disputed: R. Yehuda reads that she bore none TO HIM though she might have to another, R. Nechemya that she bore none to either.

check.note: An apparently redundant clause, verified present in the ink, read as carrying an anatomical claim; with a second dispute on the same words.

middah: E10 (the redundant she-had-no-child read — not even a place; Yevamot 64b)

claim_en: THIS UNIT'S LEDGER IS A NAMED MEMBER OF A CANONICAL CASE-TABLE ROW. The ruling counts TEN GENERATIONS from Adam to Noah and TEN from Noah to Abraham - and our 11:10-26 IS that second ten. The stated purpose is to show how long divine patience runs, 'until Abraham came and received the reward of them all'. The Mishnah's count is taken directly over this span's own steps.

check.note: A case-table row whose subject is precisely this unit's sequence of genealogical steps.

middah: plain (a teacher's statement — an identification, a narrative expansion, a recorded dispute, or the verse's own wording read as the rule; no catalogued inference form)

claim_en: THE PLACEMENT OF OUR 11:32 IS READ AS DELIBERATE NARRATIVE ORDERING, NOT CHRONOLOGY. Terach had sixty-five years still to live when Abram departed - so his death is recorded BEFORE the call although it happened after. The chain gives the reason: the wicked are called dead in their lifetimes, and the death was recorded early to spare Abram the appearance of abandoning his father. The machine's own time-anchor is thereby read as narrated out of order on purpose.

check.note: A death operator recorded before an event it followed, the ordering explained as deliberate rather than chronological.

middah: E32 (Terach's death written before the call it followed — Bereshit Rabbah 39:7)

claim_en: TWO IDENTIFICATIONS ARE MADE ON THIS LEDGER'S OWN WORDING. From our 11:29's 'father of Yiska', R. Yitzchak identifies YISKA AS SARAH - because she SAW by divine inspiration - which is how she enters the census of seven prophetesses. And our 11:28's 'Haran died אַל־פְּנֵי (al-penei) Terach' is used as the proof-text in a priestly-service dispute, R. Yitzchak reading the phrase as meaning IN HIS LIFETIME from our verse, since Haran died while Terach lived.

check.note: A person identified from this ledger's wording and thereby entered in a census, and a phrase from this ledger used as the proof-text in an unrelated priestly-law dispute.

middah: plain (a teacher's statement — an identification, a narrative expansion, a recorded dispute, or the verse's own wording read as the rule; no catalogued inference form)
